responsibility: Define how platform-specific development behavior extends the Git-generic core, including profile declaration, concept mapping, fallback behavior, evidence binding, and identifier separation without prescribing any specific hosting-platform profile.

platform_profile.description: A named declaration that maps a specific hosting platform's capabilities to the Git-generic concepts defined in phases 6-10. A profile identifies its target platform and declares which generic concepts it implements.

work_item.description: A platform-specific representation of a governing work item (e.g., GitHub issue). Work items track bounded work through its lifecycle stages.

review_proposal.description: A platform-specific representation of a review proposal (e.g., GitHub pull request). Review proposals present a set of changes for semantic review.

comment.description: A platform-specific discussion or annotation on a work item, review proposal, or specific change. Comments capture review evidence and planning records.

review.description: A platform-specific structured review of a change proposal, including reviewer identity, scope, and outcome. Review evidence is required for acceptance.

label.description: A platform-specific classification tag applied to work items or review proposals for organization, filtering, or workflow state tracking.

branch_protection.description: A platform-specific mechanism enforcing rules on branch operations, such as requiring reviews, passing checks, or limiting who can push to protected branches.

ci_check.description: A platform-specific automated check that validates code changes against defined criteria. CI results provide mechanical evidence for a specific commit.

merge_queue.description: A platform-specific mechanism for ordering and managing the integration of multiple change proposals into a target branch.

release.description: A platform-specific representation of a software release, typically tagging a specific commit with a version identifier and release artifacts.

platform_identity.description: A platform-specific user or actor identity used for attribution of work items, comments, reviews, and other platform actions.

api_evidence_reference.description: A reference to platform API artifacts that serve as evidence of platform state at a specific point in time, such as issue state, PR head, check run result, or merge commit.

profiles_declare_concept_implementation.description: A hosting-platform profile must explicitly declare which Git-generic concepts it implements. Implemented concepts may be mapped to platform-specific mechanisms.

profiles_may_not_redefine_git_semantics.description: A platform profile may extend or map Git-generic concepts but must not redefine core Git semantics such as commit, tree, branch, merge, or revision identity.

missing_capability_has_explicit_fallback.description: When a hosting platform lacks a capability expected by a generic concept, the profile must declare explicit fallback behavior. Silent omission is not permitted.

evidence_binds_to_exact_revision.description: All platform-provided evidence (CI results, review approvals, merge records) must bind to exact repository revisions. Floating-branch or non-revision-bound evidence is not acceptable.

profile_identifiers_are_not_semantic_ide.description: Platform-specific identifiers (issue numbers, PR numbers, check run IDs) are not automatically semantic identities under the framework identity model. Explicit mapping is required for identity participation.

unimplemented_concept.description: When a profile does not declare implementation of a generic concept, the framework must treat that concept's evidence as unavailable. Missing evidence blocks dependent stages.

partial_implementation.description: A profile may implement a concept partially. Partial implementation must declare which aspects are implemented and which are unavailable, with rationale.

platform_profiles_extend_generic_core.rationale: The framework defines Git-generic development concepts. Hosting-platform profiles map these concepts to platform-specific mechanisms. Profiles extend but must not redefine the generic core, ensuring portability across platforms.

evidence_binds_to_exact_revision.rationale: Platform evidence (CI results, review approvals, merge commits) must be pinned to exact repository revisions. Floating references lose auditability and undermine reproducibility.

fallback_must_be_explicit.rationale: When a platform lacks a capability, silent omission creates an incomplete evidence trail. Explicit fallback behavior ensures that missing capabilities are visible and their impact on governance stages is understood.

identifiers_are_not_semantic_identities.rationale: A GitHub issue number or PR number is a platform-specific identifier, not a framework semantic identity. Using platform identifiers as semantic identities without explicit mapping undermines the framework's platform-independent identity model.

expected_relationships: Git model (exact revision, branch, merge, commit semantics)
governed-development model (review proposal, acceptance, integration stages)
AI-continuity model (work item discovery, evidence-driven continuation)
unresolved_questions: Concrete profile declaration format and required fields are not defined.
Concept mapping serialization and validation rules are not defined.
API evidence reference format and resolution mechanism are not defined.
Fallback behavior encoding and discovery are not defined.
Multiple-profile coordination and profile layering are not defined.
